chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Social Security deduction and quitting on toilet paper
summary: Danny argued with the band's manager Steve over a twenty-five dollar Social Security deduction and handed in notice on toilet paper.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So we go to Boston, and we worked there a week. When we get paid...I can't think of the guy... Steve, who was the head of the Savoy; he runs the management. When we get paid, it's supposed to be... Payday is Sunday night, but you have to go there Monday. He gets the check, and he goes there to cash the check. So the first thing... He's just got the band and he's successful, so he's got to get a serial number from the government -- you know, the Social

Security takeout. So he went and got that, and when he come back... No... He'd taken out a hundred and a quarter. He took twenty five dollars out my money. I said, "Man, I ain't paid this much Social Security tax since I've been around." He said, "Well, Danny, I don't want to (?). I'm just keeping this in case the tax comes to that." I said, "You pay... I've got three dependents, me, my wife... And it don't come to no twenty-five dollars." So Steve came through. So I'm mad, man. He took twenty-five dollars. And I'm (?) supporting myself already. I've already sent money home, and I'm planning on maybe taking out $12, $9...

So I said, "Steve, how much money do you pay for two or three dependents? How much money?" He said, "Wait, I'll tell you." So he went and got that chart there. He said "Eleven dollars." I said, "Man, give me my money."
You told him to give you your money, huh, Danny?

So he paid me. He said, "Well, I don't like this. This is my band, and I don't know what the tax is." I said, "You heard what the man said." The rest of them is lookin' at me. And I said, "I quit." I look around, I couldn't find no pictures -- because you've got to write a written notice. I went in the toilet, got some toilet
paper, and I write: "As of now, here's two weeks notice. Danny Barker to Wilbur DeParis."
